findings.title: sanitizeTrackingParams silently drops utm_* params whose key contains malformed percent-encoding, because its key decoder diverges from queryString.parse's decoder
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §5.1: utmData is "an object holding every other param whose name starts with utm_ (i.e. excluding utm_source and utm_campaign), keyed by its param name, each value sanitized"; the helper's contract is "order comes from the raw string, values from the parse". Nothing in the spec or the approved deviations permits dropping a utm_* param that queryString.parse captures.
findings.evidence: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js:44-50 decodes each scanned key with native decodeURIComponent and falls back to the RAW key on throw; query-string v6.1.0 parse() decodes keys with decodeComponent from decode-uri-component 0.2.0 (node_modules/query-string/index.js parse(): formatter(decode(key, options), ...)), which best-effort-decodes malformed sequences instead of throwing (e.g. '%C2' -> '\uFFFD', node_modules/decode-uri-component/index.js customDecodeURIComponent). When the two decoders disagree, the occurrence-order key never matches any parse key, and utils.js:73 (parsedParams[key] !== undefined) filters the param out of utmData entirely. Empirically verified against the repo's installed libraries: sanitizeTrackingParams("?utm_x%C2=1&utm_medium=m") returns {utmData:{utm_medium:"m"}} while queryString.parse("?utm_x%C2=1&utm_medium=m") returns {"utm_medium":"m","utm_x\uFFFD":"1"} — a param whose parse-decoded name starts with utm_ is absent from utmData. Scope: only utm_* keys whose percent-encoding native decodeURIComponent rejects (decode-uri-component tries the native decoder first, so well-formed keys are identical on both paths); the param is dropped, never mis-valued, and utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref (literal names) are unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Decode the scanned key with the same decoder queryString.parse uses — e.g. import decodeComponent from "decode-uri-component" (already a transitive dependency of the pinned query-string 6.1.0) in place of the native decodeURIComponent+catch — or derive occurrence order by locating each of Object.keys(parsedParams) in the raw string, so the order-scan keys and the parse keys cannot diverge. Alternatively obtain an explicit ruling that utm_* params with malformed percent-encoded names may be dropped, and record it as an approved deviation.
